claims.author: sedited
claims.harm: Handling peer race conditions inside BaseIndex couples indexing code to P2P transport concerns and risks stalls in other callers
claims.quote: Reading through this, I don't think this should be handled on the index level.

status_by.quote: Added deferring of a response, we store the racing request in a PendingCFilterRequest struct in a Peer and then check it

claims.status_note: author moved the handling out of the index into net_processing

claims.author: ajtowns
claims.quote: The benchmarking commit should be removed, not squashed, presumably? It doesn't seem like it'll be useful beyond developing this PR?
claims.request: Remove the benchmarking commit instead of squashing it, and mark PR as draft while commits need replacing

claims.author: ajtowns
claims.quote: Rather than an optional, I'd suggest considering std::list<PendingCFilterREquest> and using push_back to add requests to the end
claims.request: Use std::list instead of std::optional for pending cfilter requests to handle multiple requests and save memory

status_by.quote: Changed an optional in favor of a list with up to MAX_PENDING_CFILTER_REQUESTS=2 entries.

claims.status_note: switched to std::list with a limit

claims.author: mzumsande
claims.harm: Touching index internals violates separation of concerns when GetSummary already exposes sufficient state
claims.quote: Races in net_processing shouldn't be the business of indexes, and GetSummary() should have enough info... so I'd prefer if the index code was not touched at all

status_by.quote: Removed IsRacing, now using GetSummary. No changes in GetSummary were required.

claims.status_note: author removed IsRacing and used GetSummary without touching index code

claims.author: ajtowns
claims.harm: Handle getcfheaders and getcfcheckpt the same as getcfilters since disconnects happen frequently for getcfheaders
claims.quote: Based on the logs in #29655 this seems backwards -- there were more disconnects for getcfheaders than getcfilters? So I think this ought to be handled for all the cases?

status_by.quote: Yes, all three cbf messages should be handled the same way.

claims.status_note: author agreed that all three messages should be handled identically

claims.author: ajtowns
claims.quote: I wonder if it wouldn't be better to adopt the "pause this peer" approach, rather than queueing messages but continuing.
claims.request: Pause the peer entirely on a pending cfilter request instead of queueing cfilter responses and continuing to process other messages

status_by.quote: I took some time to gain more understanding on how net_processing works and your comments make a perfect sense.

claims.status_note: author adopted the approach on top of ajtowns' branch and benchmarked it
